books.title: Firefighters
books.art_why: Modern firefighters, fire trucks, helicopters and fireboats all exist today, so real photographs are possible.

pages.text: Introduction Can you hear the loud siren? It is the sound of firefighters rushing to fight a fire in their bright red fire truck. Firefighters put out fires and save people whose lives are in danger. They also help prevent fires from starting. They inspect buildings, and they teach people about fire safety.
pages.brief: A bright red fire truck races down a street with its siren sounding and firefighters in helmets riding it on the way to a fire. Nearby, other firefighters walk through a building making an inspection and stand before a group of people teaching them about fire safety.

pages.text: What Makes Fire Burn Fires need both fuel and oxygen to burn. Some types of fuel are wood, oil, and coal. Oxygen is a gas in the air. The more fuel or oxygen there is, the hotter the fire will burn. Different kinds of fires are stopped in one of three different ways. One is to remove the fuel, and a second way is to smother the fire by removing its oxygen. A third way is to remove the fire’s heat with water. Do You Know? In our solar system, Earth is the only planet where fire can burn. Earth is the only planet with enough oxygen. Even a candle can’t burn without it.
pages.brief: A small flame burns on a candle, with wood, oil and coal stacked nearby as fuel and air all around. One fire is smothered so no oxygen can reach it, and water is poured on another to take away its heat.

pages.text: Types of Fires Firefighters put out house fires, factory fires, and forest fires. They must be prepared to fight many different kinds of fires and face other dangers, too.
pages.brief: Three fires burn in one scene: a house with flames coming from its windows, a factory with fire inside, and a forest where flames move between the trees. Firefighters in helmets and heavy gear stand ready with hoses, prepared for each one.

pages.text: Firefighting Equipment Firefighters use many different tools to fight fires. Large hoses spray water or special foam on fires, and tall ladders reach high places. Axes chop holes in doors, roofs, and walls to reach places safely.
pages.brief: Firefighters work with their tools: two of them hold a large hose that sprays water or foam, while a tall ladder rises up the side of a high building. Another firefighter swings an axe to chop a hole in a door.

pages.text: Smoke masks and air tanks protect firefighters from smoke, and large fans remove smoke from rooms. Firefighters also use fire extinguishers to put out small fires.
pages.brief: Firefighters wear smoke masks and carry air tanks on their backs as they move through a smoky room. A large fan blows the smoke out of the room, and one firefighter points a fire extinguisher at a small fire.

pages.text: Firefighting Machines Fire trucks are an important firefighting machine, and there are four main kinds. The most common, a pumper truck, carries long hoses and a pump to spray water a long way.
pages.brief: A pumper truck, the most common kind of fire truck, stands on a street with its long hoses unrolled and stretched along the ground. A pump on the truck sends water a long way from it.

pages.text: Other kinds of fire trucks include ladder trucks, tanker trucks, and rescue trucks. Ladder trucks carry ladders of many different sizes. Big ladder trucks have a ladder that can reach up to ten stories high.
pages.brief: Three trucks stand together: a ladder truck with ladders of many different sizes, a tanker truck and a rescue truck. On the biggest ladder truck a long ladder reaches up and up, as high as ten stories of a building.

pages.text: Tanker trucks carry water to fight fires in places without water. Rescue trucks carry equipment to help rescue people who are trapped. There are other kinds of firefighting machines, too. Fireboats fight fires from the water by pumping water from under the fireboats and spraying it on the fire.
pages.brief: A tanker truck stands at a fire in a place with no water supply. A rescue truck carries equipment for freeing people who are trapped. Out on the water, a fireboat pumps water from beneath itself and sprays it onto a fire.

pages.text: Helicopters dump water on fires in places that trucks cannot reach. Large planes help fight forest fires, too. Sometimes planes dump chemicals instead of water to slow the spread of a forest fire.
pages.brief: A helicopter carries water and dumps it on a fire in a place that trucks cannot reach. Above a forest fire, a large plane drops chemicals instead of water to slow the fire's spread.

pages.text: Becoming a Firefighter You must be at least eighteen years old to be a firefighter. Before you can become one, you must pass a written test and a fitness test. You must be in very good shape to fight fires. Firefighting school trains people to fight different kinds of fires. They also learn how to rescue people and how to treat them if they’re hurt.
pages.brief: Firefighters must be at least eighteen years old, so trainees study hard and train to stay in very good shape for a written test and a fitness test. At firefighting school they learn to fight different kinds of fires, rescue people and treat them if they are hurt.

pages.text: Conclusion Fire is useful, of course. Scientists think that people have been using it to cook for more than four hundred thousand years. Fires can keep us warm in the winter, and some forests need fire to stay healthy. At the same time, fire can be very dangerous to people and other living things. Every year, fire takes many lives and destroys large areas of forest.
pages.brief: People cook food over a fire and sit beside a fire to keep warm in winter, and flames move through the undergrowth of a forest. Fire is useful, but it is dangerous too, taking many lives and destroying large areas of forest every year.

pages.text: A Fierce Fire In 1666, the Great Fire of London destroyed most of the city. It also helped end an outbreak of the plague. The fire killed the rats and fleas that carried and spread the deadly illness. Fires also destroy thousands of buildings. Long ago, fires burned down entire cities because there was no way to stop them from spreading. Today, we have brave firefighters to put out fires and help keep us safe.
pages.brief: In 1666 flames sweep through the crowded streets and wooden buildings of London, destroying most of the city. The rats and fleas that carried the plague die in the fire. Long ago fires burned whole cities because nothing could stop them spreading; today firefighters put fires out.

books.title: Martin Luther King, Jr.
books.art_why: Named famous person biography.

pages.text: Growing Up in the South Each year in January, we celebrate Martin Luther King Day. We remember the life and work of a great leader. Who was he? Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. was born on January 15, 1929. Where King grew up, white leaders made unfair laws. They took many rights away people. They segregated, or apart.
pages.brief: A cartoon view of Martin Luther King Jr. as a young boy growing up in the South. People in January remember his life and work. White leaders are shown making unfair laws that take rights away and keep Black and white people segregated, or apart.

pages.text: Many places, such as schools, bathrooms, parks, and waiting rooms were segregated. The places for Black people were not as nice or clean as those for white people. Black people couldn’t live in white neighborhoods. They couldn’t marry a white person. As King grew up, he saw how these laws hurt Black people. He wanted to help.
pages.brief: A cartoon scene showing segregated schools, bathrooms, parks and waiting rooms, with Black people’s places less nice or clean than white people’s. Black people cannot live in white neighborhoods or marry a white person. Young Martin Luther King Jr. sees how these laws hurt Black people and wants to help.

pages.text: King Goes to School King started college at the age of fifteen. He decided to become a minister. At school, King learned about a leader in India who used peaceful protest to help people. King decided to use peaceful protest, too. After King finished school, he and his wife moved to Alabama. He became a minister there. Coretta Scott King King’s wife was Coretta Scott King. She was an important leader. She started a center to teach people how to protest peacefully. She also helped make her husband’s birthday a holiday. She died in 2006.
pages.brief: A cartoon of young Martin Luther King Jr. starting college at fifteen and deciding to become a minister. He learns about an Indian leader who used peaceful protest. After school, he and his wife Coretta move to Alabama, where he becomes a minister. Coretta is an important leader who starts a peaceful-protest center and helps make his birthday a holiday.

pages.text: Protest in Montgomery In 1954, the U.S. Supreme Court ended segregation in schools. Black people hoped this meant other places wouldn’t be segregated anymore. In 1955, a Black woman named Rosa Parks was riding a city bus in Montgomery. Black people had to sit at the back of the bus. They had to give up their seat to a white person if asked. Parks knew this was unfair. A white man asked for her seat. She didn’t move. The police arrested her.
pages.brief: A cartoon of the U.S. Supreme Court ending segregation in schools in 1954. In 1955 Montgomery, Rosa Parks rides a city bus and sits where Black people are forced to sit. A white man asks for her seat. She does not move, and police arrest her.

pages.text: After Parks was arrested, Black people protested. They stopped riding segregated buses. They put King in charge of the protest.
pages.brief: After Rosa Parks is arrested, a cartoon shows Black people protesting by refusing to ride segregated buses in Montgomery. They stand together instead of boarding. The protestors put Martin Luther King Jr. in charge of the bus protest.

pages.text: A year later, buses were no longer segregated. The protest had worked. It showed that things could change. It helped King become a well-known leader. The Women of the Bus Protest Black women played an important part in the bus protest. Even before 1955, Black women were working for change in Montgomery. Women helped the protest keep going. They held meetings, planned carpools, and talked to protestors. Their work helped the protest succeed.
pages.brief: A year later, a cartoon shows buses no longer segregated and the protest having worked. The bus protest helped Martin Luther King Jr. become a well-known leader. Black women are shown holding meetings, planning carpools and talking to protestors; their work helps the protest keep going and succeed.

pages.text: The Birmingham Protests White people who were angry about desegregation bombed King’s house. This didn’t stop King. In 1963, King started a protest in Birmingham, Alabama. Hundreds of people were arrested during the peaceful protest, including King. Black leaders raised money to get protestors out of jail. At another march the next protestors. The fire hoses and attack dogs. Many of the were hurt.
pages.brief: A cartoon of angry white people bombing Martin Luther King Jr.’s house, but King continues his work. In 1963 in Birmingham, Alabama, King starts a peaceful protest. Hundreds are arrested, including King, and Black leaders raise money to get protestors out of jail. At another march, fire hoses and attack dogs hurt many protestors.

pages.text: When people across the country saw what happened to the protestors, they were angry. Black civil rights leaders and city leaders made a deal a week later. Birmingham would desegregate. People Who Inspired King Dr. Benjamin Mays (1894–1984) Mays was a minister and the president of the school King attended. He became a teacher to King. Howard Thurman (1899–1981) Thurman was a minister and King’s teacher at school. He taught King about peaceful protests. Mohandas Gandhi (1869–1948) Gandhi was a leader in India. His ideas about peaceful protest inspired King. Bayard Rustin (1912–1987) Rustin was a leader and King’s friend. He helped organize a famous march in Washington, D.C., in 1963.
pages.brief: A cartoon of people across the country seeing what happened to the protestors and feeling angry. Black civil rights leaders and city leaders make a deal: Birmingham will desegregate. Nearby are four people who inspired King: Benjamin Mays, Howard Thurman, Mohandas Gandhi and Bayard Rustin, shown as a teacher, minister, Indian leader and friend.

pages.text: The Work Continues King organized more marches and gave a famous speech. He called for equality for all people. The next year, the president of the United States made segregation against the law. The fight for civil rights was not over, though.
pages.brief: A cartoon of Martin Luther King Jr. organizing more marches and giving a famous speech calling for equality for all people. The next year, the president of the United States makes segregation against the law. The fight for civil rights is not over, though.

pages.text: In 1965, King helped plan a march to protest how Black voters were treated in Alabama. King led the protestors. They didn’t get far before police attacked them. Three weeks later, the protestors marched again. This time, members of the U.S. Army sent by the president protected the protestors.
pages.brief: In 1965, a cartoon shows Martin Luther King Jr. helping plan a march in Alabama to protest how Black voters are treated. King leads the protestors, but police attack them before they get far. Three weeks later, the protestors march again, and U.S. Army members sent by the president protect them.

pages.text: On August 6, 1965, the president signed the Voting Rights Act into law. It protected the right of all people of color to vote. The Right to Vote All Black people had the right to vote by 1920. State laws made it hard for them to vote, though. Black voters were forced to take unfair tests or pay money before they could vote. Sometimes white people attacked Black people if they tried to vote. Congress passed the Voting Rights Act to help fix these problems. It helped. Lawmakers changed the law in 2013. The change allowed state leaders to pass new voting laws. Some say the laws keep voting fair. Others say the laws make it harder for Black people and other people of color to vote.
pages.brief: A cartoon of the president signing the Voting Rights Act on August 6, 1965, protecting people of color’s right to vote. Black voters face unfair tests and money demands before Congress passes the law. Later, lawmakers change the law in 2013 as state leaders pass new voting laws; people disagree whether these laws keep voting fair or make it harder.

pages.text: King’s Memorial In 1968, a white man shot and killed King in Tennessee. King died on April 4. People around the world were shocked and sad about his death. In 2011, a memorial for King opened in Washington, D.C. People from all over the world visit it and remember him. They carry on the work for justice and equality.
pages.brief: A cartoon of a white man shooting and killing Martin Luther King Jr. in Tennessee in 1968; King dies on April 4. People around the world are shocked and sad. In 2011, a memorial for King opens in Washington, D.C., where people from all over the world visit, remember him and carry on the work for justice and equality.

books.title: Blackbeard the Pirate
books.art_why: Blackbeard lived three hundred years ago, so no photograph of him or his ships is possible.

pages.text: The Man Behind the Stories Picture a pirate in your mind. Do you think of a cartoon pirate with a beard, an eye patch, and a parrot? Three hundred years ago, real pirates did sail the seas. One pirate had a name that scared everyone. He was known as Blackbeard.
pages.brief: An imagined pirate stands on a ship's deck with a beard, an eye patch and a parrot on his shoulder. Behind him, real pirate ships with dark sails ride the sea three hundred years ago, and one big bearded captain stands at the rail.

pages.text: Becoming Blackbeard Blackbeard’s real name was Edward Teach. He was born in England about 1680. When he was old enough, Teach learned to sail a ship. England was at war. Teach joined the crew of a ship that attacked enemy ships to help the English navy. Soon, he decided it would be better to join a pirate crew, instead! NORTH AMERICA West Indies CENTRAL AMERICA.
pages.brief: A young Edward Teach in England, about 1680, learns to handle ropes and sails aboard a wooden ship. English warships fire on enemy vessels at sea, and Teach stands among the crew watching before he later joins a pirate crew on a rougher deck.

pages.text: The leader of the pirate crew put Teach in charge of a pirate ship. They attacked so many other ships that everyone was afraid of them. Why did sailors become pirates? In those days, sailors worked very hard but made very little money. When a country was at war, any ship might be hired to attack and steal enemy ships. It was dangerous work. The hired sailors were paid a small reward for the ships or treasure they took. Pirates could attack any ship—even one from their own country! Pirates could keep all the ships and treasure for themselves!
pages.brief: Teach stands on the deck of a pirate ship, put in charge by the pirate leader, while his crew attacks another vessel and hauls away treasure. Tired sailors work hard for little pay, and hired armed crews chase enemy ships for a small share of what they seize.

pages.text: One day, Teach and his pirate crew captured a large, fast, French ship. The pirate leader gave the ship to Teach as a reward. Teach added more cannons to make it a very dangerous ship. Then he gave his ship a new name—the Queen Anne’s Revenge. The Queen Anne’s Revenge and Teach soon became very famous. No ship wanted to see the fast ship and its black pirate flag chasing them. Edward Teach was now Blackbeard, the pirate. The Golden Age of Piracy During the 1700s, European countries set up new towns in the Caribbean and North and South America. English, French, Dutch, and Spanish cargo ships sailed back and forth. They were easy targets for pirates.
pages.brief: A large, fast French ship is captured and handed to Teach as a reward. Sailors add more cannons on deck, and the ship is renamed the Queen Anne's Revenge. It chases a merchant ship, its black pirate flag flying, while cargo ships sail between new Caribbean and American towns.

pages.text: Blackbeard Ruled the Sea Blackbeard scared everyone who saw him. He was a huge man with a thick, braided, black beard. He stuck burning fuses in it. This made his beard look as if it was on fire.
pages.brief: Blackbeard stands on his ship, a huge man with a thick, braided black beard. Burning fuses are stuck in the beard, smoking and glowing so it looks as if it is on fire. Sailors on a nearby deck stare at him in fear and back away.

pages.text: Blackbeard soon had four fast ships and a crew of over 350 men. One time, his four ships sailed to Charleston, South Carolina. They robbed every ship sailing in or out of Charleston. Pirate’s Life for Me? How did Blackbeard get such a big crew? Pirates often shared treasure with their crews. Most sailors got little pay. If a pirate attacked their ship, sailors often chose to join the pirates! Some enslaved people joined the pirates as a way to escape slavery.
pages.brief: Four fast pirate ships carrying over 350 men sail to Charleston, South Carolina, robbing ships going in and out of the harbour. On deck, treasure is shared out among the crew, and sailors from captured ships, including enslaved people escaping slavery, choose to join the pirates.

pages.text: Sailing a large ship close to the land is hard to do. The water isn’t very deep. One day, Blackbeard and all of his men were sailing home with their treasure. Blackbeard sailed the Queen Anne’s Revenge too close to the land. His ship got stuck in the sand near a town on the coast called Beaufort. Blackbeard told his men to move the treasure onto the other ships. He dropped off many of his men on a nearby island. Then, Blackbeard sailed away, taking the loot with him. Had he wrecked his ship on purpose so he could keep the treasure for himself?
pages.brief: The Queen Anne's Revenge lies stuck in the sand near Beaufort, close to shore where the water is shallow. Blackbeard's men carry treasure across to the other ships, and many men are left on a nearby island. The other ships sail away with the loot.

pages.text: Virginia Bath North Carolina Beaufort South Carolina Charleston Georgia North Carolina Bath Florida Beaufort Beaufort Inlet.
pages.brief: A wide coastal view of the southeastern coast, from Virginia down through North Carolina, South Carolina and Georgia to Florida. Shorelines, inlets and rivers weave along the land, and Beaufort sits beside the water where the ship ran aground, with the inlet opening to the sea.

pages.text: Blackbeard’s Last Fight For a time, it seemed that Blackbeard had stopped being a pirate. He got married and bought a house. People stopped worrying about him. Blackbeard soon went back to his old life, though. He went to sea in his last ship, the Adventure. Blackbeard began attacking other ships again.
pages.brief: Blackbeard on land, married and settled in a house, while people around him go about their business no longer worrying about him. Then he returns to the sea in his last ship, the Adventure, standing on deck as his crew attacks another vessel again.

pages.text: The governor of Virginia was tired of Blackbeard’s attacks. He sent a fighting ship called the Ranger to find and capture Blackbeard. One morning, the crew of the Ranger saw the Adventure near the island of Ocracoke.
pages.brief: The governor of Virginia, tired of the attacks, sends the fighting ship Ranger to find Blackbeard. One morning the Ranger's crew sight the Adventure near Ocracoke island, the two ships close together on the water, cannons ready, men watching from the decks.

pages.text: The two ships fought, firing their cannons for many hours. In the heavy smoke from the cannon fight, the Ranger’s crew hid. They made it seem as though they had been killed. Blackbeard thought he had won, so he climbed onto the Ranger. The Ranger’s crew jumped out from their hiding places and the fight began again. Blackbeard fought hard, but the Ranger had too many men. He was shot five died. The Ranger’s Blackbeard’s the sea.
pages.brief: The two ships fire cannons for many hours, smoke rolling across the water. The Ranger's crew hide and seem to have been killed; Blackbeard climbs aboard, and they leap out to fight again. Outnumbered, Blackbeard is shot five times and dies at sea.

pages.text: Blackbeard Sailed Into History Blackbeard’s true story may be behind the colorful pirates in many books and movies. The next time you hear a pirate story, remember one real pirate in history: Blackbeard!
pages.brief: Shelves of books and a screen showing colourful pirate tales, with bearded captains, parrots and treasure, sit beside the memory of the real Blackbeard, his dark ship and black flag, remembered as one pirate in history.

pages.text: The capital of Kenya is Nairobi. More than three million people live there. The city has many businesses. Many different goods are made there. Nairobi has many hotels for people who visit Kenya. At one famous hotel, guests can eat breakfast with giraffes! Nairobi became the capital of Kenya in 1907. Kenya.
pages.brief: Nairobi is Kenya’s capital, a city of more than three million people. Many businesses operate there and many different goods are made. The city has many hotels for people who visit Kenya. At one famous hotel, guests can eat breakfast with giraffes.

pages.text: Dancers from different tribes celebrate Kenya’s freedom on December 12. People from Kenya celebrate many. Great Britain ruled Kenya for many years. On December 12, 1963, Kenya became a free country. Every December 12, people celebrate with feasts, parades, and dancing.
pages.brief: Dancers from different Kenyan tribes celebrate Kenya’s freedom on December 12. They dance together in a parade, marking the day Kenya became a free country in 1963 after years of British rule. Around them, people celebrate with feasts, parades, and dancing.

pages.text: Some tribes in Kenya raise camels to race and to carry people. Kenya’s camel race festival starts in late. It lasts for three days. People come from all over the world to race. At the festival, enjoy bike races, dancing, and local. They buy arts and crafts made by different tribes. Kenya.
pages.brief: Some tribes in Kenya raise camels to race and to carry people. At Kenya’s camel race festival, camels run as people from all over the world take part. The festival lasts three days and includes bike races, dancing, and local arts and crafts made by different tribes.

pages.text: (Main) Zebras and a giraffe drink from a water hole in a protected area in Kenya. (Inset) Lions also live in these protected areas. Kenya is famous for its wild animals. Some of them are very. Kenya has more than fifty parks and areas for animals. Every year, many people travel to Kenya to see these animals. Giraffes, zebras, and other grazing animals fill Kenya’s and cheetahs live on the savannas, too.

Cheetahs live on the savannas, and Kenya has more than fifty parks and areas for animals. Many people travel to Kenya each year to see these animals.

pages.text: Hippos may look cute, but they can be dangerous. Elephants, buffalo, and rhinos also live. Crocodiles and hippos swim in its rivers and lakes. Kenya has more than a thousand kinds of birds. Wading birds live near lakes. Eagles and hawks glide through the air. Kenya.

books.title: Magnetism
books.art_why: A science and technology topic using real objects and machines is best shown with photographs.

pages.text: Look around your home and try to find a magnet. A magnet is a metal object that sticks to other metals. You might have some magnets among your toys. There are probably magnets on your refrigerator. But did you know that there may be hundreds of magnets in your home? You cannot see most of them. But they are inside your television, telephone, and stereo. They are inside electric motors that power your blender and hair dryer. Computers are full of magnets. And all the electricity that runs these things comes from magnetism.
pages.brief: A home scene shows a magnet on a refrigerator and toy magnets among toys. Cutaway views reveal hidden magnets inside a television, telephone, stereo, blender, hair dryer, and computer. Electricity and magnetism are linked to these everyday objects.

pages.text: Magnetism and Magnets Magnetism is an invisible force. A force is anything that pushes, pulls, or moves an object. Magnetism is a special force that only pulls on some metals, such as iron. A magnet will not push or pull plastic or tin. Magnetism flows in one direction through a magnet, no matter what shape the magnet is. It flows in one end and out the other. The ends of a magnet are called magnetic poles. Every magnet has a north and a south pole. The force flows out the north pole and back in the south pole.
pages.brief: A magnet attracts iron objects but leaves plastic and tin untouched. A visible flow of magnetic force travels in one end of the magnet and out the other. At the ends are a north pole and a south pole, showing the force's direction through the magnet.

pages.text: You can use two magnets to feel magnetism flowing. The north pole of one magnet will stick to the south pole of the other. Now, try to push the two north poles together. It feels almost like trying to connect two hoses that are both spraying water. The magnetic force pushes the north poles apart, because the magnetic forces are flowing against each other. Two north poles will always repel each other. So will two south poles.
pages.brief: Two magnets are held so a north pole meets a south pole and they stick together. Then two north poles are pushed toward each other and resist, like two hoses spraying water against each other. The magnetic forces flow against each other, so the north poles repel.

pages.text: The Earth’s iron core is magnetic. The whole planet acts like a giant magnet. If you dangle a magnet by a string, one pole will point north and the other will point south. This is exactly of a magnet their names. Do You Know? Earth’s north and south magnetic poles are not quite at the true North and South Poles. The north magnetic pole is in northern Canada. The south magnetic pole is in the Pacific Ocean south of Australia. Since Earth’s core moves around, the magnetic poles move, too. They can even flip completely around. If this happened today, your compass needle would point south!
pages.brief: Earth appears as a giant magnet with its iron core inside. A magnet hanging from a string points one pole north and the other south. The north magnetic pole lies in northern Canada; the south magnetic pole is in the Pacific Ocean south of Australia. These magnetic poles move and can even flip.

pages.text: The magnetic force flows out the north pole of the magnet. Then, it loops around outside the magnet and flows back in the south pole. Magnetism flows through space in lines of force. The invisible shape formed by the lines of force around the magnet is called the magnetic field.
pages.brief: Magnetic force flows out of a magnet's north pole, loops around through space, and returns into the south pole. The invisible lines of force form a curved shape around the magnet. This surrounding shape is the magnetic field.

pages.text: Any iron or other magnets inside a magnetic field will be pulled toward the magnet. Stronger magnets have more lines of force and larger magnetic fields. To see a magnetic field, place a magnet on a piece of paper. Sprinkle iron filings around the magnet. The filings will gather along the lines of force in the shape of the magnetic field.
pages.brief: A magnet lies under a sheet of paper, and iron filings sprinkled around it gather along invisible lines of force. The filings reveal the shape of the magnetic field. A stronger magnet would show more lines of force and a larger field, pulling iron toward it.

pages.text: How Are Magnets Made? The first magnets were made of a natural rock called lodestone. People used pieces of lodestone in compasses. But they did not know how they worked. Every material is made of extremely tiny atoms. Most atoms spin. This a tiny, tiny force. In most things, like rocks or plastic, the atoms spin every which way. The tiny forces never add up. But when something becomes magnetized, the atoms spin in the same direction. All the tiny forces add up to create a magnetic force. Eventually, people learned how to line up the atoms in some metals to create new magnets.
pages.brief: A piece of natural lodestone rock sits beside an early compass. Tiny atoms spin in many directions in ordinary rock or plastic, so their tiny forces do not add up. In magnetized metal, the atoms spin in the same direction, and their forces combine into magnetism.

pages.text: Some things, such as iron, become magnetized more easily than others. A piece of ordinary iron is placed inside a strong magnetic field. The magnetic force makes the iron atoms line up and spin in the same direction. This makes a new magnet. The more atoms that spin in the same direction, the stronger the magnet becomes. Sometimes if you drop a magnet, some of the atoms get knocked out of line, and the magnet gets weaker.
pages.brief: A piece of ordinary iron is placed inside a strong magnetic field. The magnetic force makes the iron atoms line up and spin in the same direction, creating a new magnet. Dropping the magnet can knock atoms out of line and make it weaker.

pages.text: Make your own magnet! Try This You will need a large iron nail, a strong magnet, and several paper clips. Hold the nail by one end and slide it across 1. the magnet in one direction. Keep sliding it over and over. The magnet’s lines of force will start to line up the atoms in the nail. 2. After 20 to 30 times, touch the nail to the paper clips. Does the nail pick up the clips? How many can it pick up at once? Keep stroking the nail along the magnet to make the nail’s magnetic force stronger. See if you can pick up all the paper clips at once.
pages.brief: A large iron nail is slid across a strong magnet in one direction, again and again. After twenty to thirty strokes, the nail touches several paper clips and picks them up. Continuing to stroke the nail along the magnet makes its magnetic force stronger.

pages.text: Magnetism and Electricity Magnetism and electricity are very closely related. Magnets can make electricity. And electricity creates magnetic fields. This is because both magnetism and electricity affect the way atoms spin.
pages.brief: A magnet and an electric current are shown side by side, linked by the way both affect spinning atoms. Magnets can make electricity, and electricity creates magnetic fields. The picture connects magnetism and electricity as closely related forces with a shared effect on atoms.

pages.text: All the electricity you use comes from machines called generators. Generators make electricity by spinning magnets around coils of wire. The magnetism creates an electric current in the wire. The difficult part is getting the magnets spinning. Power plants use running water, wind, or steam from burning fuel to turn the magnets.
pages.brief: A generator uses spinning magnets around coils of wire to make electricity. The magnetism creates an electric current in the wire. At a power plant, running water, wind, or steam from burning fuel turns the magnets, which is the difficult part of making electricity.

pages.text: Electricity can create special magnets called electromagnets. A wire is wrapped around a regular piece of iron. Then an electric current from a battery or outlet flows through the wire. The electric current makes a magnetic field. This magnetizes the iron. But the iron only stays magnetized as long as the electricity is on.
pages.brief: A wire is wrapped around a regular piece of iron and connected to a battery. Electric current flows through the wire, creating a magnetic field that magnetizes the iron. This special electromagnet stays magnetic only as long as the electricity is on.

pages.text: The earliest use of magnetism was the compass. A small, freely moving magnetic needle pointed to Earth’s magnetic north pole. This helped guide travelers and explorers. Modern travelers still use compasses. Electricity comes from spinning magnets inside generators. And electric motors work like generators in reverse. They use electric current to spin magnets. The magnets are attached to fans, cutting blades, or wheels. This is how fans, blenders, and remote-control cars work.
pages.brief: An early compass with a freely moving magnetic needle points toward Earth's magnetic north pole, guiding travelers and explorers. Nearby a modern compass is shown. Spinning magnets inside generators make electricity, while electric motors use current to spin magnets attached to fans, blender blades, and remote-control car wheels.

pages.text: Magnets can also encode information, or store it in a special code. Hotel key cards and credit cards use strips of tiny magnets. The magnets are the size of grains of powder. There can be millions of magnets on one key card or credit card. Each tiny magnet points in its own direction. The different positions of the magnets create a code. Credit card and hotel door readers sense the tiny magnetic fields and read the code. Putting a credit card or key card near a powerful magnet can mess up or erase the code.
pages.brief: A hotel key card and a credit card show strips of tiny magnets the size of powder grains. Millions of these tiny magnets point in different directions, creating a code. A card reader senses their magnetic fields and reads the code; a powerful magnet nearby can erase it.

pages.text: Some high-speed trains run on electromagnets. The trains have powerful electromagnets on the bottom. The track also has powerful electromagnets. The two electromagnets face each other so that they repel each other. The magnetic force is so strong that it lifts the train off the track. The train floats above the track. It actually flies as it travels. This makes a fast, smooth ride.
pages.brief: A high-speed train has powerful electromagnets on its bottom, and the track has powerful electromagnets too. The matching electromagnets face each other and repel, lifting the train off the track. The train floats and flies above the track, making the ride fast and smooth.

pages.text: Special machines called MRIs can look inside a person’s body. The person lies inside a tube cut right down the center of a very powerful magnet. The lines of force flow through the person’s body. The magnetism is so strong that it causes the atoms in the body to spin in the same direction. Special sensitive instruments can tell how fast the atoms spin. Computers figure out what kind of atoms they are based on how they spin. This gives doctors an idea of what is going on inside a person’s body. Doctors can find atoms that are not supposed to be there. They can see cancer and other give doctors a look inside the having to cut the body open.
pages.brief: A person lies inside a tube cut through the center of a very powerful magnet. Magnetic lines of force flow through the body and make its atoms spin in the same direction. Sensitive instruments measure how fast the atoms spin, and computers help doctors look inside without cutting the body open.

pages.text: While magnets may seem simple, there is no end to their uses. Every time you watch a tape, turn on the air conditioner, or even turn on a light, you are using magnets. Someday you may ride on a high-speed train or use an MRI. Playing with magnets can be lots of fun. The magnetism you play with is the same force that has made modern life possible.
pages.brief: Everyday uses of magnets surround a scene: a tape playing, an air conditioner running, a light turned on, a high-speed train, and an MRI machine. Playing with magnets is shown as fun. The same magnetism that is fun to play with has made modern life possible.
